note: mapping_basis=data_labels, and there is no mapping step to get wrong. data/comeau_2015_energy_literacy.py melts the .sav with d.melt(id_vars=['id'], value_vars=cols, var_name='item') and renames nothing, so the live IRW item code IS the source column name, which is the key the SPSS variable label is stored under. item_text is that variable label; option_text is the same column's SPSS value labels. Two deliberate, recorded edits to the label string, neither touching a word the respondent read: the SPSS variable tag SPSS itself prepends ([q7.0], [Q21.0]) is stripped, and the questionnaire's emphasis markup (<u>LEAST ENERGY</u> in q29, <u>impossible</u> in q31) is reduced to its words. Each shipped table is exactly one battery, so where all its items share one stem that stem is recorded once in instructions and the item-specific half of the label (after the ' | ' the deposit uses) is item_text; section_id and section_prompt are unused. The script already asserts every item in a table shares one value-label set, so one option block per table is correct, and the option rows are restricted to the codes that actually occur in the shipped table rather than every code the label set defines. LANGUAGE, open question: the administration was probably not English-only.
